title: One facade module is the only place the D1 binding is read
asA: developer who needs the domain code to stay swappable and testable across the persistence boundary
iWant: one facade module to hold the D1 binding and expose named domain verbs, with no consumer reaching into env for the binding directly
soThat: the boundary between the domain and the D1 vendor surface is the only place that has to move when the vendor changes and the only place tests have to double

acceptanceCriteria.description: Exactly one source-tree module reads the D1 binding from the Worker `env`. Every other module that touches persistence imports the facade module and calls its named domain verbs.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the running source tree after a Worker request is handled
acceptanceCriteria.when: the import graph and source tree are inspected for the D1 binding reference (`env.<BINDING_NAME>` where BINDING_NAME is the value configured on `d1_databases[].binding` in the project's wrangler config)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the reference appears in exactly one file (the facade module) and no other file in the source tree contains the reference, verified by an import-graph query or a targeted grep against the configured binding name

acceptanceCriteria.description: The facade exposes named domain verbs for every persistence operation the domain requires; the facade module does not export the raw D1 binding or a general-purpose query method that accepts a raw SQL string from consumer code.
acceptanceCriteria.then: every exported symbol is either a named domain verb with typed parameters or an event-sink registration; no exported symbol is the D1 binding itself, and no exported function accepts a raw SQL string as a call argument from consumer code

acceptanceCriteria.description: Replacing the facade module with an in-memory double that implements the same verb surface allows the domain code to run against it without any reference to the D1 binding.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a test double implementing the same named verbs as the facade with an in-memory backing store
acceptanceCriteria.when: the domain code runs against the double in place of the facade
acceptanceCriteria.then: the domain code executes to completion with no reference to the D1 binding on its call path, and its behaviour is unchanged from a facade-backed run for the operations under test
